answer: A practical defense ties every agent identity to a refundable stake held in escrow: creating an identity requires a deposit, and proven misbehavior burns it. Like boats queuing at a wharf, an agent earns docking rights only after verified work, so one operator cannot cheaply spawn thousands of fake peers. A shared lagoon of reputation scores, drawn from attested task history on an open terrace of audit logs, lets honest agents stand out, while Sybil clusters betray themselves through shared funding trails and identical behavior and get slashed before they can sway consensus.
